trial_court: District Judge, Alipore, Matrimonial Suit No. 217 of 1993
case_name: Smt. Chandrima Guha vs Sumit Guha
facts_of_case: Husband filed suit for divorce on ground of exceptional hardship under Section 13(1)(ia) of Hindu Marriage Act; wife alleged to be upstart and ultra-modern lady causing mental and physical agony and torture.

legal_principles.principle: The factual allegations in a particular case must make out a case of extraordinary hardship to entitle the applicant to a leave under Section 14(1) of the Act.
legal_principles.held: The circumstances must be unusual. Applying the said ratio, in the instant case, we do not find that the grant of leave can be justified.
cited_cases: Rabindra Nath Mukerjee v. Iti Mukherjee, (1991) C.L.J. 209

legal_principles.principle: The allegations in an application for leave under Section 14(1) of the Act must be tentatively sufficient to uphold a prayer for a decree for divorce.
legal_principles.held: The allegations, which though tentatively sufficient for upholding a prayer for a decree for divorce, may not necessarily constitute exceptional hardship within the meaning of the said section.
cited_cases: Rabindra Nath Mukerjee v. Iti Mukherjee, (1991) C.L.J. 209

outcome.final_order: Leave under Section 14(1) of the Act granted without affording opportunity of being heard to respondent; allegations constituted exceptional hardship within meaning of section.
